findings.summary: When no boundary is in the buffer yet, last_newline() returns index 0 (the leading CRLF), which is never deleted, so with chunked input the CRLF can leak into the field value.
LINE_BREAK_RE.match(data) is used without a None check, so if the buffer doesn't start with a line break, .end() raises AttributeError instead of a clean ValueError.
The encoder writes the CRLF between headers and body only when the first Data event is non-empty, so if the decoder emits an empty first Data(b"", more_data=True), the CRLF is lost on re-encode.
